lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Animal Babies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about animal offspring from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about an animal baby.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap animal offspring names from Year 1 (calf, lamb, piglet).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about animal offspring.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: What is this baby animal called?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about animal offspring.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about an animal baby at home.

lessons.title: Counting Animal Offspring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and represent numbers of animal offspring to 100.
success_criteria: I can count offspring in a group.
I can represent the number using tens and ones.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting groups of animal offspring counters, representing with tens and ones.
lessons.independent_task: Children count and represent animal offspring quantities using base-10 blocks.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record place value consolidation applied to a science context — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count a group of toy animals at home.

lessons.title: Animal Offspring Grow into Adults
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe that animal offspring grow into adults.
success_criteria: I can name a baby animal and its adult form.
I can describe how it changes.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss baby animals and their adult forms known.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss that offspring grow and change into adults, using clear examples (puppy to dog, chick to hen).
lessons.independent_task: Children match baby animals to their adult forms, describing changes.
resources_needed: Baby and adult animal picture cards
key_questions: What does this baby animal grow into?

differentiation.greater_depth: Match 6+ pairs and describe changes in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of growth from offspring to adult — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a pet or animal you've seen grow.

lessons.title: Writing About an Animal Life Cycle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing stages of an animal life cycle in order.
success_criteria: I can write about a life cycle stage.
I can use sequencing words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the chicken life cycle from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing sentences describing life cycle stages in order using sequencing words.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing an animal's life cycle in order.

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied sequencing vocabulary

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing writing skill applied to science — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share life cycle sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe an animal life cycle to your family.

lessons.title: Multiplication: Groups of Eggs/Offspring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve multiplication problems using an animal offspring context.
success_criteria: I can multiply using equal groups.
I can write the multiplication sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving multiplication problems using an offspring context (e.g. 4 nests with 3 eggs each).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve multiplication problems using counters, recording sentences.

differentiation.support: Use counters for 2 and 10 times tables

lessons.assessment_notes: Record multiplication application to a science context — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Find equal groups of animal toys/pictures at home and multiply.

lessons.title: The Butterfly Life Cycle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence the life cycle of a butterfly.
success_criteria: I can order the butterfly life cycle stages.
I can name each stage.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about butterflies/caterpillars.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the butterfly life cycle (egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly) using a diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence and label butterfly life cycle picture cards.

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence and explain all 4 stages independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note life cycle sequencing understanding for a new example — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the butterfly life cycle sequence.
lessons.home_link: Look up the butterfly life cycle together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Life Cycle Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read life-cycle-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read life cycle words.
I can read a sentence about a life cycle.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to life-cycle-themed words (e.g. 'egg', 'grow', 'hatch').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading life cycle words over the week.

lessons.title: Division: Sharing Offspring Fairly
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve division problems using an animal offspring context.
success_criteria: I can share into equal groups.
I can write the division sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving division problems using an offspring context (e.g. sharing 20 chicks between 5 hens).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve division problems using counters, recording sentences.
key_questions: How many each if shared equally?

differentiation.support: Use counters for division by 2 or 10

lessons.assessment_notes: Record division application to a science context — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing objects equally at home.

lessons.title: The Frog Life Cycle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence the life cycle of a frog.
success_criteria: I can order the frog life cycle stages.
I can name each stage.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about frogspawn/tadpoles.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the frog life cycle (spawn, tadpole, froglet, frog) using a diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence and label frog life cycle picture cards.

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence and explain all 4 stages independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note life cycle sequencing understanding for a third example — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the frog life cycle sequence.
lessons.home_link: Look up the frog life cycle together.

lessons.title: Presenting a Life Cycle
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present an animal life cycle clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can explain the life cycle stages in order.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all life cycles studied this week (chicken, butterfly, frog).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a life cycle.
lessons.independent_task: Children present a chosen animal life cycle to a small group, answering a question.
resources_needed: Life cycle diagrams from the week

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific sequencing skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Explain a life cycle to your family.

lessons.title: Life Cycle Data: Comparing Stages
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the number of stages in different life cycles using a chart.
success_criteria: I can record the number of stages.
I can compare life cycles.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the three life cycles studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recording the number of stages for each life cycle in a simple chart, comparing.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a chart comparing life cycle stages and answer questions.
key_questions: Which life cycle has the most stages?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note data handling applied to comparing scientific information — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap the life cycle comparison chart.
lessons.home_link: Compare two life cycles with your family.

lessons.title: Comparing Life Cycles
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare similarities and differences between animal life cycles.
success_criteria: I can say a similarity between two life cycles.
I can say a difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the three life cycles studied.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing life cycles (e.g. all start with an egg, but stages differ).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare two life cycles, recording similarities and differences.
key_questions: What is similar about these life cycles?

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative scientific reasoning — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Compare two animal life cycles with your family.

lessons.title: Animal Life Cycles Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about animal life cycles.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's life cycle learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about animal life cycles, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What comes after the caterpillar stage?
Why might a frog need to live in water as a tadpole?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on life cycle facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Multiplication, Division, Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply multiplication, division and data skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can multiply and divide using equal groups.
I can compare data in a chart.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of multiplication, division, and data handling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: multiplication/division, data handling.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 21 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N3/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising multiplication and division over the weekend.

lessons.title: Animal Offspring and Life Cycles Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about animal offspring and life cycles.
success_criteria: I can name an animal life cycle.
I can sequence its stages.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering offspring, growth, and the three life cycles studied.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Life Cycles' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about life cycles?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note life cycle understanding progress, setting up healthy eating/exercise next week — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's life cycles learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about life cycles with your family.
